description: Mercimek Corbasi is a beloved Turkish red lentil soup, renowned for its creamy texture and comforting warmth. This vibrant, wholesome soup is a staple in Turkish homes, often enjoyed as a starter or a light meal. Its rich flavors, enhanced by a fragrant butter and mint drizzle, make it an unforgettable culinary experience.

instructions.title: Prepare Lentils and Aromatics
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear; drain well. Finely chop the onion and mince the garlic, preparing them for sautéing.

instructions.title: Sauté Vegetables
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, which usually takes about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.

instructions.title: Build Flavor Base
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2-3 minutes, allowing it to deepen in color and flavor. This step is crucial for a rich base. Add the rinsed and drained red lentils, stirring to combine them with the aromatics and tomato paste.

instructions.title: Simmer the Soup
instructions.text: Pour in the vegetable or chicken stock and water. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have completely broken down.

instructions.title: Blend to Creaminess
instructions.text: Remove the pot from heat. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup directly in the pot until it is completely smooth and creamy. If you dont have an immersion blender, carefully transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth, then return it to the pot.

instructions.title: Prepare the Topping (Sos)
instructions.text: In a small pan, melt the butter over medium-low heat. Add the dried mint and red pepper flakes (pul biber) and cook for 30 seconds to 1 minute, until fragrant. Be vigilant not to burn the butter or spices, as this can make them bitter.

instructions.title: Serve and Garnish
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into individual bowls. Drizzle each serving generously with the fragrant butter and mint topping. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side for squeezing, as the lemon juice adds a wonderful brightness and tang to the soup.

tips: For a Smoother Texture: To achieve the signature velvety texture of Mercimek Corbasi, ensure you blend the soup thoroughly with an immersion blender. If using a regular blender, blend in batches and be cautious with hot liquids.

The Flavor of Pul Biber: The red pepper flakes, known as "pul biber" in Turkish, are crucial for an authentic taste. They offer a mild, fruity heat; adjust the quantity to your spice preference for the perfect balance.

Serving with Lemon: Always serve Mercimek Corbasi with fresh lemon wedges. A squeeze of lemon juice brightens the flavors and adds a zesty tang that perfectly complements the rich, earthy lentils, elevating the entire dish.
article:
Discovering the heart of Turkish cuisine often begins with a bowl of soup, and among the myriad of comforting options, Mercimek Corbasi (Red Lentil Soup) stands out as a true culinary icon. This vibrant, wholesome, and incredibly flavorful soup is more than just a dish; it's a staple, a source of warmth, and a taste of home for millions. From bustling street vendors to elegant restaurant tables, and especially within every Turkish household, Mercimek Corbasi holds a cherished place. Its simplicity belies a depth of flavor that is both nourishing and deeply satisfying, making it a beloved starter, a light meal, or a comforting antidote to a chilly day.

## What is Mercimek Corbasi?

Mercimek Corbasi is a creamy, bright red lentil soup that embodies the essence of Turkish comfort food. Unlike some more elaborate Turkish soups, it’s known for its relatively straightforward preparation and universally appealing taste. At its core, it’s made from humble red lentils, which cook down to a wonderfully smooth consistency. The magic, however, lies in the carefully balanced aromatics and spices: typically onions, garlic, tomato paste, and a generous flourish of dried mint and chili flakes (pul biber) infused in sizzling butter or oil, drizzled just before serving.

This soup is a testament to the Turkish philosophy of making simple ingredients shine. It’s often served with a wedge of lemon, whose fresh, zesty squeeze brightens the earthy lentil base and elevates every spoonful. While often enjoyed as a starter in restaurants, it’s hearty enough to be a light lunch and is even a popular breakfast item in many parts of Turkey, providing a nutritious and energizing start to the day. The vibrant red hue of Mercimek Corbasi is as inviting as its aroma, promising a delightful experience that is both healthy and deeply satisfying.

## Ingredients for Turkish Red Lentil Soup

The beauty of Mercimek Corbasi lies in its accessible and wholesome ingredients. You don't need exotic spices or hard-to-find produce to create this authentic Turkish delight. Here’s what you’ll typically need:

*   **Red Lentils:** The star of the show. Split red lentils cook quickly and break down easily, giving the soup its characteristic creamy texture.
*   **Onion & Garlic:** The aromatic foundation. Finely chopped onion and minced garlic provide a sweet and pungent base that deepens the soup's flavor.
*   **Tomato Paste (Salça):** A crucial ingredient in Turkish cooking. It adds a concentrated tomato flavor, a touch of sweetness, and contributes to the soup's beautiful color.
*   **Water or Vegetable Broth:** The liquid base. Broth will add more depth, but water is perfectly acceptable and traditional.
*   **Dried Mint (Kuru Nane):** An essential herb for Turkish red lentil soup. Its distinctive aroma and flavor are key to the soup's authentic taste.
*   **Pul Biber (Aleppo Pepper Flakes):** These mild, flavorful chili flakes provide a gentle warmth and a beautiful red color to the butter drizzle.
*   **Butter or Olive Oil:** Used for sautéing the aromatics and, crucially, for creating the flavorful mint and chili infused drizzle that crowns the soup.
*   **Flour (Optional):** A small amount of flour can be used to thicken the soup slightly, creating a roux with the butter and tomato paste. Many recipes omit it for a naturally thickened, lighter soup.
*   **Salt & Black Pepper:** To season to taste.
*   **Lemon Wedges:** For serving, an absolute must for that final zing.

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Mercimek Corbasi

Making Mercimek Corbasi is a straightforward process, even for beginner cooks. Here's a typical approach to creating this delicious Turkish red lentil soup:

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any starch and ensures a cleaner flavor. You don't typically need to soak red lentils as they cook quickly.
2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat a tablespoon or two of olive oil or butter over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.
3.  **Add Tomato Paste and Flour (if using):** Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly. This step "cooks out" the raw flavor of the tomato paste and deepens its color. If using flour, sprinkle it over the aromatics and tomato paste, stirring constantly for another minute to create a light roux.
4.  **Incorporate Lentils and Liquid:** Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot, stirring to combine them with the aromatics. Pour in the water or vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have started to break down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
5.  **Blend the Soup:** Once the lentils are tender, remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup directly in the pot until it's completely smooth and creamy. Alternatively, you can transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender (be very cautious with hot liquids – fill the blender only halfway and hold the lid down with a towel).
6.  **Season and Adjust Consistency:** Return the blended soup to the stove over low heat. Season generously with salt and black pepper to taste. If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot water or broth until it reaches your desired consistency.
7.  **Prepare the Chili-Mint Drizzle:** While the soup is simmering or after blending, prepare the flavorful topping. In a small pan, melt 2-3 tablespoons of butter over medium-low heat. Once the butter is melted and slightly foamy, add the dried mint and pul biber. Sauté for about 30 seconds to a minute, just until fragrant, being careful not to burn the spices.
8.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into bowls. Drizzle a spoonful of the fragrant chili-mint butter over each serving. Garnish with a fresh lemon wedge on the side.

## Tips for the Best Mercimek Corbasi

Achieving that perfect, authentic Mercimek Corbasi isn't difficult, but a few key tips can elevate your soup from good to unforgettable:

*   **Rinse Your Lentils Thoroughly:** This is crucial. Rinsing removes excess starch, which can make the soup cloudy and sometimes give it an undesirable flavor. Keep rinsing until the water runs clear.
*   **Cook the Tomato Paste:** Don't just dump it in. Sautéing the tomato paste for a minute or two with the onions and garlic "cooks out" its raw flavor, deepens its color, and concentrates its sweetness, adding a richer base to your soup.
*   **Blend Until Silky Smooth:** For that classic creamy texture, blend the soup until there are no visible lentil pieces. An immersion blender makes this quick and easy, but a regular blender works just as well (exercise caution with hot liquids).
*   **Don't Skip the Drizzle (Tereyağlı Sos):** The melted butter infused with dried mint and pul biber is not merely a garnish; it's an integral part of the Mercimek Corbasi experience. It adds an incredible aroma, a beautiful color, and a layer of rich, savory flavor that completes the dish.
*   **Fresh Lemon Juice is Essential:** Always serve Mercimek Corbasi with fresh lemon wedges. A generous squeeze of lemon juice stirred into each bowl just before eating cuts through the richness, brightens all the flavors, and adds a delightful tang. It's truly non-negotiable for an authentic taste.
*   **Adjust Seasoning:** Taste and adjust salt and pepper as needed. Lentils absorb a lot of salt, so don't be shy, but add gradually.
*   **Quality Pul Biber:** If possible, use authentic Turkish pul biber (Aleppo pepper flakes). It has a unique fruity, mild heat that is distinct from generic red pepper flakes.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings

Mercimek Corbasi is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in many ways. Traditionally, it's served hot, fresh from the pot, with minimal fuss.

*   **Lemon is Key:** As mentioned, a generous wedge of fresh lemon is the most common and essential accompaniment. Squeeze it directly into your bowl just before you eat.
*   **Crusty Bread:** A slice of warm, crusty bread, like Turkish pide or a simple baguette, is perfect for dipping and soaking up every last drop of the flavorful soup.
*   **Fresh Herbs:** A sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley or mint can add a touch of freshness and color, though it's less common than the dried mint in the butter drizzle.
*   **Alongside Main Courses:** In Turkey, Mercimek Corbasi often serves as a comforting starter to a larger meal. It pairs beautifully with grilled meats like kebabs, chicken dishes, or even vegetable stews.
*   **As a Light Meal:** With its wholesome ingredients, this soup is hearty enough to be a satisfying light lunch or dinner on its own, especially when accompanied by bread and a simple salad. A classic pairing would be a fresh shepherd's salad (çoban salatası) with tomatoes, cucumbers, and onions.
*   **Yogurt (Optional):** While not traditional for red lentil soup, some people enjoy a small dollop of plain yogurt stirred in for extra creaminess and a tangy contrast.

## Variations & Dietary Adaptations

One of the great things about Mercimek Corbasi is how naturally accommodating it is to various dietary needs and how easily it can be adapted.

*   **Vegetarian/Vegan:** The basic Mercimek Corbasi recipe is already naturally vegetarian. To make it vegan, simply use olive oil instead of butter for both sautéing and the final drizzle. Ensure your vegetable broth (if using) is vegan-friendly.
*   **Gluten-Free:** If you omit the optional flour used for thickening, Mercimek Corbasi is naturally gluten-free. Always double-check labels on tomato paste and broth to ensure they are certified gluten-free if you have a severe intolerance.
*   **Adding Vegetables:** While traditional Mercimek Corbasi focuses on lentils, you can easily add other vegetables for extra nutrition and texture. Finely diced carrots, potatoes, or celery can be added along with the onions and cooked until soft before blending. This will make the soup even more substantial.
*   **Spicier Version:** If you love heat, increase the amount of pul biber in the butter drizzle, or add a pinch of hotter red pepper flakes. You could also incorporate a fresh finely diced chili pepper with the garlic.
*   **Herb Variations:** While dried mint is classic, don't be afraid to experiment. A pinch of dried oregano or thyme can add a different aromatic note, though it will steer slightly away from the traditional Turkish flavor profile.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** For a subtle smoky depth, a tiny pinch of smoked paprika can be added along with the tomato paste.

Mercimek Corbasi is more than just a soup; it's an embodiment of Turkish hospitality and culinary tradition. Its comforting warmth, vibrant flavors, and nutritious profile make it a dish that transcends borders and brings a taste of Turkey right into your home. Whether you're seeking a quick, healthy meal or a comforting starter, this red lentil soup is a perfect choice that promises to delight your senses and nourish your soul. Give it a try, and discover why Mercimek Corbasi has remained a beloved classic for generations.
